transcript: calling all eldest daughters I have found our play I'm an eldest daughter my mother is an eldest daughter and liberation by Bess wohl understands that relationship in a way I've never seen on stage before if you're an eldest daughter you know this but we wear many hats caretaker mediator role model and we have very specific relationships with our mothers and one thing liberation really digs into is is how well can you ever truly know your mom and if you met her before she had you would you even recognise her? Susannah Flood is the narrator a daughter who has recently lost her mother that's only after her mother is gone that she learns the history of who her mother was she wants to learn more and she does this by embodying Lizzie her mother in the 1970s and in the 1970s Lizzie has recently started a feminist group it is this tight knit group of women who want to change the world and how women are seen they have very different philosophies do this Isidora who's from Sicily wants to burn the whole place down Margie who's been a housewife all of her life just wants her husband to do the dishes and then there is Celeste the only black woman in the group who has gone from being a radical in the city to a caretaker to her ailing mother liberation does not shy away from the way that black women have been failed and continue to be failed by the women's liberation movement my friend Kaisha @KaishaCreates I'll tag her in the caption did an incredible video on Liberation on this topic specifically you should go watch it but ultimately to me this is a show about a daughter trying to understand her mother and therefore understand herself and the play is about the choices that you make and the ones you don't and how you come to terms the things you will just never know and to my eldest daughters I see you need you to see liberation
